sacellum, sacellī n.

noun, second declension

a small shrine; a chapel

Classically a small place sacred to a god; Morgan–Owens finds it for a chapel in Dante and Egger.

Other words

  • ōrātōrium, ōrātōriī n. — a place of prayer, an oratory

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Jdt. 9.1: Judith ingressa est ōrātōrium suum; Aug. Ep. 109 (Lewis & Short)

    Any place set aside for prayer, such as a room in a house or a monastery (M-O).

  • capella, capellae f. — chapel

    noun, first declension · avoid · medieval · M-O s.v. chapel, after Latham and Niermeyer

    Classically a little she-goat (īte domum saturae, venit Hesperus, īte capellae, Verg. Ecl. 10.77). The medieval word for a chapel comes from cappa, the cape of St Martin kept in such a shrine, and only looks the same; sacellum says it in classical Latin.

Examples

  • est ad hanc manum sacellum: ibi angiportum propter est

    on this side there’s a little shrine; right by it there’s an alleyTer. Ad. 576

See also church, monastery.

SourcesLewis & Short: sacellum · Lewis & Short: oratorius · Lewis & Short: capella
